items.finding: Although block scaling is commonly suggested when combining data, in certain cases it can degrade outcomes compared with alternative preprocessing approaches.
items.how_it_applies: When planning laboratory data fusion from the two instruments, one should compare block scaling against other preprocessing routines rather than assuming it is optimal.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited review focuses on dairy applications, so behavior may differ on model biological tissue matrices and ATR or fluorescence signals.

citation.quote: While block scaling is often recommended for data fusion, sometimes it can have a worse effect on results than other pre-processing methods (17).
citation.label: E02 ¶16

items.finding: Prior to combining datasets from multiple measurement sources, assessing each dataset's individual contribution and complementarity is crucial.
items.how_it_applies: The experimental plan should evaluate separate single-method performance to verify genuine complementarity before committing to a fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This review paper discusses general PAT applications, and observed benefits or lack of complementarity depend heavily on the specific analytical targets and tissue samples.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82
